newsitem.title: JAPAN: MOF's Ogawa says raising taxes not easy option.
newsitem.headline: MOF's Ogawa says raising taxes not easy option.

text.p: Japan will not easily resort to raising taxes as it tries to reduce its fiscal deficit, Vice Finance Minister Tadashi Ogawa told reporters on Thursday.
"I strongly think that we should not easily lean toward asking the public to bear more of a tax burden," Ogawa said when asked how Japan was going to go about reducing its fiscal deficit.
He urged for a review of revenue and spending at both local and central government levels and make necessary reforms to achieve its deficit-cutting goals.
The government will first aim at cutting down general spending, he said.
Ogawa declined to comment on specific market levels when asked about the weak yen and the recent sharp fall in Tokyo stock prices.
He said the government must closely monitor the economy when it is either rising or falling too rapidly.
Ogawa reiterated his view that the economy seemed to be improving a little.
